sections.heading: How to Play Elemental
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Elemental"][color=c7]Elemental Shaman Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_shaman_maelstromweapon size=medium type=round color=c7 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=shaman]Avoid Maelstrom waste:[/color][/b] This resource  enables us to cast our spender spenders, such as [spell=61882] and [spell=8042] or [spell=117014], so waste as little as possible.[/td]
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_nature_lightning size=medium type=round color=c7 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=shaman]Always Be Casting:[/color][/b] Elemental Shaman lacks mobility cooldowns and tools for "quiet movement". As such it is not just important to know when you can move, it is also very important to know when you can either start moving early, or even better just not move at all. Utilize all your utility spells, such as [spell=378081] and [spell=79206] as much as possible and try to get your group to set up external mobility spells like [spell=374968].[/td]
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_shaman_lavasurge size=medium type=round color=c7 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=shaman]React to procs:[/color][/b] Elemental's has a few proc that can lead to moments of high damage or grant access to buffs to other spells. Namely, [spell=114050] strongly buffs spells cast during its duration, so syncing your cooldowns and pooling resources like [resource=11] or [spell=454009] procs is important here. On the other hand, [spell=77756] procs give access to [spell=16166] which should be spent on your highest damage spells like e.g. [spell=454009].[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c7][icon name=spell_nature_lightning type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon] Elemental Shaman Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Elemental has access to a variety of different cooldowns on its spec tree. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers [i]how[/i] they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Stormkeeper" icon=ability_thunderking_lightningwhip]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_thunderking_lightningwhip type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Stormkeeper [/color][/h3]

[spell=191634] is our main short cooldown spell. For [spell=188196] it increases the damage of the next 2 casts by 150% and force it to trigger one additional overload. For [spell=188443] it does not directly increase the damage, but instead triggers an additional overload on every target hit.

The tier set improves this cooldown to instead buff the next 3 casts by an extra 25% up to 175% for Lightning Bold and 25% for Chain Lightning and also giving some Haste whenever you activate the cooldown.

Try to sync this with [spell=114050], which buffs the resulting overloads quite substantially.[pad]

In addition to the aformentioned points, for [color=necrolord]Farseer[/color] this cooldown also spawns an Ancestor, significantly increasing the effective damage done by this cooldown.
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Ascendance" icon=spell_fire_elementaldevastation]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_fire_elementaldevastation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Ascendance [/color][/h3]

[spell=114050] casts [spell=470411] on up to 6 enemies within range that you are in combat with. While active, it buffs your Overloads by 75% and makes all spells that can overload do so exactly one additional time. For [spell=188443] this means that you get one additional overload on the main target of the cast.

If you are specced into [spell=378255] this spell also spawns a [spell=198067], which buffs the duration and tick rate of [spell=188389]. Be aware that the Elemental is only active after the initial Flame Shocks are applied, so you need to make sure to cast another Flame Shock in the GCD at the end of the duration of the Elemental but after the Ascendance expired.

Make sure to use spells that trigger more overloads or more spells that can overload before you go into Ascendance, like [spell=191634] and [spell=470057] (if in AoE and specced into [spell=1259471]).
[pad]
[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c7][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon] Elemental Shaman Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]


[pad]
[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Farseer AoE" icon=ability_racial_ancestralcall]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c7] Farseer AoE [/color][/h3]
	Farseer relies on the damage down by the Ancestors spawned whenever you press either [spell=191634] or [spell=443454]. In general, the Ancestors are duplicating your spell casts in that they cast [spell=447419] whenever you cast a "Single-Target" spell, and [spell=447425] whenever you cast an "AoE" spell. The classification for "Single Target" and "AoE" is pretty intuitive and would exceed this little tip box, but it is important to note that fundamentally only "actual spell casts" trigger the Ancestors. If you cast a spell such [spell=51505], your Ancestors will also send a Single Target [spell=447419], but any overloads on that spell will be ignored by them. The exception to this rule are all spells that trigger [spell=188389] to be applied to enemies. For some reason, these are still reacted to by the Ancestors, triggering a Lava Burst on each target.

	So what does this mean rotationally?

	Always try to line up your [spell=114050] and [spell=470057] right after you cast your Stormkeeper and Ancestral Swiftness, but try to cast the Voltaic Blaze outside of the Ascendance window. In other words your burst window should look like this:

	Stormkeeper>>Ancestral Swiftness>>Voltaic Blaze>>Ascendance.
[/tab]
[tab name="What is RNG?" icon=inv_misc_dice_01]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c7]How does Randomness work for Elemental? [/color][/h3]
	Most, if not all, random procs in the spec rely on a system commonly known as "Deck of Cards". In summary, random procs like [spell=454009] or [spell=443445] use very strong bad luck protection, forcing a certain amount of successes within a certain amount of "attempts", normalizing proc rates and limiting variance.

	Playing around these mechanics and effectively "predicting" random procs during normal gameplay can lead to notable DPS increases but usually requires external tools to simplify tracking of the actual proc chances at any given moment.

	With the changes to addons, it has becomes significantly hard to do so, but by no means impossible. While currently there are no addons available that implement this functionality for Elemental, it is only a matter of time.

	On a similar note, while to our knowledge [spell=77756] doesn't use this explicit deck system, its procs are also strongly normalized and can effectively be predicted during normal gameplay. This knowledge can be very helpful to achieve very minor DPS gains via [spell=16166] allowing players that are very comfortable and used to the spec to hold [resource=11] when they can "feel" a proc coming, and on the other hand, hold a Lava Surge proc for a while, because for the first 3 or so seconds, it is effectively impossible to immediately get another proc and overwrite the existing one.
[/tab]
[tab name="Purging Flames Optimization" icon=inv12_ability_shaman_purgingflames]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c7]How do I minmax my damage with Purging Flames? [/color][/h3]
	For a very unintuitive "trick" and tip we can take a look at the functionality of [spell=1259471]. This spell makes it so that your next [spell=51505] is "echoed" at up to 5 other targets that are not your main target with an active [spell=188389]. Because the echoes are limited to a number lower than the active Flame Shocks and cant hit your main target, a weird little quirk appears where if you fight a number of enemies and you have less than 6 Flame Shock active, but you have at least one extra target without a Flame Shock, then casting Lava Burst against this target becomes optimal.

	As an example, if you are fighting 6 targets and you only hit 5 of those with your [spell=470057], if you then cast your Lava Burst against a target with Flame Shock, you get your main cast and 4 "echoes", one per other target with a Flame Shock. If you instead cast the Lava Burst against the target without a Flame Shock, you get your main cast which loses its guaranteed crit, and then you get 5 "echoes" instead.

	All in all, this is very situational, and should not be played around by most people, but if you are desperate for ways to minmax, this is one of the possible ways to do so.
